sampling_model.design: A fixed finite population is partitioned into \(m\) labeled clusters; the chosen law \(D\) randomizes jointly over cluster saturation labels and exact treated subsets.
sampling_model.units: Potential outcomes \(Y_{g i}(z,a)\) are fixed; there is no superpopulation sampling.
sampling_model.treatment: Cluster \(g\) receives label \(A_g\), then exactly \(r_{s_g,A_g}\) of its \(s_g\) units are treated.
sampling_model.overlap: The general results allow every feasible count \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant menus. Interiority is imposed only for the stated forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes; saturation variation is imposed only for the last two. Optimal designs may assign zero probability to labels or assignment orbits.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the estimator is chosen jointly with the randomization and may be nonlinear in the revealed outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 derives standard errors and power criteria for individual saturation and slope effects under a clustered regression model.
Theorem 1 shows that independent fair assignment with a nonlinear estimator is minimax over bounded no-interference potential outcomes.
Theorem 2.3 Bernoulli-lifts the binary no-interference minimax experiment to bounded outcomes and decodes a nonlinear rule.
Proposition 2.2 expresses the arbitrary-neighborhood-interference minimax risk as a function of a pairwise conflict graph.
The paper optimizes bias and variance of the difference-in-means estimator across randomized saturation designs under a linear interference model.
Theorem 2.1 proves minimax complete randomization by group averaging under permutation invariance for a fixed invariant estimator.

body.tldr: Randomized saturation experiments expose overlapping vectors of own-treatment-by-saturation responses, so their unrestricted design-and-estimation problem is neither the no-interference tensor product nor a pairwise conflict-graph game. For fixed saturation count and bounded cluster size, every feasible treated-count table, including boundary counts and a constant treated-count menu, admits an exact reduction of worst-case mean squared error over all correlated designs, bounded schedules, and measurable estimators to a rational endpoint orbit game. Conditional uniform subset randomization is without loss, and independent-saturation minimaxity has a finite primal-dual characterization. Interiority is confined to the forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes, while saturation variation is confined to the last two; the rational two-cluster, size-three certificate gives a strict correlated-saturation advantage on an infinite rational contrast neighborhood. The central open task is a complete polynomial Turing bit-complexity proof, including coefficient construction, weak conic optimization, outward-rounded certificates, and total nonlinear-estimator decoding on zero-mass faces.

project_justification.gap: Saturation-design papers optimize power or the bias and variance of specified regression or inverse-probability estimators, while recent unrestricted minimax papers either assume no interference or replace observation feasibility by a pairwise conflict graph. None preserves the exact-count observation hypergraph while jointly optimizing the first-stage law and an arbitrary measurable estimator across the full feasible menu, including zero, full, and label-constant treated counts.
project_justification.niche: Fixed saturation-label count and bounded cluster size leave exponentially many labeled schedules but only polynomially many size-tagged response, assignment, and observation histograms, whether treated counts are interior, on the boundary, or constant across labels. That symmetry permits an exact decision-theoretic quotient without assuming independence or linearity.
project_justification.fill: The paper establishes endpoint completeness and a stabilizer-weighted rational primal-dual orbit game for every feasible count table, with implementable correlated randomization and nonlinear estimation; it then gives a general finite independent-design frontier, confines interiority to the higher-order obstruction, equality witness, and strict rational separation certificate, and confines saturation variation to the last two, while exposing bit complexity and zero-face decoding as the open task.

body.related_work: BairdBohrenMcIntoshOzler2018 supplies the application-facing direct and spillover design tradeoff, but its Theorem 1 optimizes regression-based precision rather than unrestricted bounded-schedule risk; the general orbit result also covers pure-control, pure-treatment, and label-constant exact-count menus. HudgensHalloran2008 and JiangImaiMalani2023 establish randomization-based estimands, unbiased estimators, variances, and inference for two-stage designs; they do not choose a minimax nonlinear procedure. AronowSamii2017 gives the design--exposure--estimand factorization and exact joint exposure-probability bookkeeping used to define the observation channel. BasseFeller2018 makes unequal cluster sizes and person-versus-cluster weighting explicit. Bai2023 and Kallus2021 motivate group symmetrization and mixed designs, but do not construct the saturation response kernel or certify its bit complexity. Hull2026 and SudijonoDobribanTchetgenTchetgen2026 solve closely related unrestricted bounded no-interference games; their independence conclusion depends on a tensorized observation channel. KandirosHarshawSavje2026 studies unrestricted network-experiment minimax risk through a pairwise conflict graph, whereas Theorem 2 proves that the interior size-three fixed-count slice has an irreducible triple obstruction. CaiPougetAbadieAiroldi2022 shows that interference changes desirable saturation dispersion under a linear model and fixed estimator; Theorems 3 and 4 instead compare independent and correlated label laws while allowing every measurable estimator. Interiority is confined to the obstruction, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry instances, and saturation variation to the latter two.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact arithmetic verifier confirms the 78-decision upper procedure, the 17-orbit unrestricted lower certificate, the 15-orbit independent lower certificate, and all 333,336 binary response orbits. A separate labeled enumeration for cluster sizes \((3,3,4)\) matches the size-tagged orbit kernel and normalizes to one for all six assignment histograms under the checked treated-count table. These are presolve diagnostics, not proofs of the general orbit theorem or the Turing bit bound.
body.honest_scope: Endpoint completeness, finite minimax duality, the orbit formulas, and conditional uniformity hold for every feasible table \(0\le r_{q,a}\le q\), including boundary counts and menus constant across labels. The finite independence criterion has the same general scope. Interiority is used only for the forbidden-triple, strict-separation, and complement-symmetry regimes, and saturation variation only for the last two. The full Turing bit-complexity and total zero-face decoder are exposed in \(\texttt{oeq:bit-certified-compiler}\) as the first-class open content. The paper does not claim an elementary closed-form classification of the independence frontier, a separation with the number of clusters tending to infinity, or exact rational optimizers. The complement-symmetry proposition supplies the required equality reduction.
